status_summary: H.R. 7, the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act of 2025, was introduced on 2025-01-22, and the Conscience Protection Act of 2025 was introduced as S. 1756 and H.R. 3411 on 2025-05-14; the Senate HELP Committee held a hearing on S. 1756 on 2026-03-19, and none of the bills has passed either chamber. Executive Order 14182 (signed 2025-01-24) revoked two 2022 orders on reproductive health care access but does not codify Hyde. An HHS notice cites the Weldon Amendment as section 507(d) of Division B of Public Law 119-75, the fiscal year 2026 appropriations law enacted 2026-02-03, so Weldon continues as an annual appropriations rider; annual riders are not the permanent codification the text asks for and are not counted toward the stage.

timeline.event: H.R. 7, the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act of 2025, was introduced in the House.
Executive Order 14182, Enforcing the Hyde Amendment, was signed; it revokes Executive Orders 14076 and 14079, directs OMB guidance, and does not codify Hyde.
The Conscience Protection Act of 2025 was introduced in the Senate as S. 1756 and in the House as H.R. 3411.

The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, H.R. 7148), including the Labor, HHS and Education appropriations division, was enacted (date from a GovInfo margin note); it carries the annual Weldon provision as section 507(d) of Division B per an HHS notice, which is a one-year rider rather than permanent law.
The Senate HELP Committee held a hearing on S. 1756, the Conscience Protection Act of 2025; no markup or floor action followed in the bill status record.

title: Codify the Hyde amendments and the Weldon Amendment in permanent law
uncertainties: Bill titles, numbers, sponsors, introduction dates and action histories were read on GovInfo, including the bill status records, which show no action after referral for H.R. 7 and H.R. 3411 and a committee hearing for S. 1756. The enactment date of Public Law 119-75 was read from a margin note on the GovInfo page and the Division B text was beyond the part of the page that could be read, so the continued presence of the Hyde provisions in the FY2026 law was not confirmed directly; the Weldon citation comes from the HHS OCR notice at 91 FR 39626. A web search found advocacy letters asking Congress to eliminate the Weldon Amendment in the FY2027 bills, read only as leads. Related OCR conscience enforcement is tracked in c14-09, the Hyde travel funding record in c14-20, and the broader Hyde and conscience items in c00-09.
